clue.text: Fear of a god

definitions.meaning: relating to Pan, the Greek god of the wild, whose shout was said to cause sudden terror

explanation.definitionFit: Sudden terror is the everyday sense; the capitalised adjective means belonging to the goat-footed Greek deity Pan.

clue.text: Talks at length, or repeats parts

indicators.note: parts as a verb means separates, so the letters of the two words are split up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone speaks long-windedly or keeps repeating sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun but is the verb that breaks up OR REPEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: To perorate is to make a long, formal speech, holding forth.

clue.text: Point to Strangelove as a subject for this

definitions.text: Point to Strangelove as a subject for this

parts.note: N, north, is a compass point

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the four letters following it are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Suggesting Dr Strangelove as the theme for a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Strangelove is a film, so the solver reads one name; 'Strange' must be split off as the anagram signal for the rest, and the whole clue doubles as the definition, love being a classic theme for fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is a typical subject for a work of long prose fiction.

clue.text: Businesses include service with bill of sale for pipes

indicators.note: the two firms include, that is hold within them, the naval abbreviation

parts.note: two businesses are two companies, CO and CO
RN, the Royal Navy, is a service
B/S is the commercial abbreviation for bill of sale

explanation.surface: Companies take on a service along with a sales document for tobacco pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Corncobs are tobacco pipes with bowls made from dried maize cobs.

clue.text: Former Chinese capital can be liable to taxation

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of the word Chinese is taken

parts.note: 'can' read as 'is able' gives the two words is able

explanation.surface: A one-time Chinese capital city might be subject to tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese capital' looks like a city such as Nanking, but 'capital' just means the initial letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Excise is a duty charged on goods, so something excisable can have that duty levied on it.

clue.text: Prophet has not succeeded as a writer

indicators.note: has not means the prophet's name lacks the letter for succeeded

parts.note: Elias is the Greek form of the prophet Elijah
s is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A prophet failed in his career as an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Elia was the pen name of Charles Lamb, author of the Essays of Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb wrote his essays under the pseudonym Elia.

clue.text: Jargon I gloat over in this kind of bridge

parts.note: cant is the jargon of a particular group

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word for gloat is read backwards

parts.note: to revel in something is to gloat over it

explanation.surface: Gloating over jargon about bridge construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns REVEL into LEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever bridge is built of projecting arms anchored at one end only.

clue.text: Sausage consumed by journalist on motorway

parts.note: George Augustus Sala was a famous Victorian journalist
the M1, written MI, is Britain's first major motorway

explanation.surface: A banger eaten by a reporter driving on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London-to-Yorkshire motorway, its digit read as letter I; George Augustus Sala was a celebrated Victorian reporter. 'consumed by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured Italian sausage, usually eaten sliced.

clue.text: Not much of a game

definitions.meaning: a trifle, something of little importance
a table game in which balls are knocked into holes on a board

explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is both a trifling thing and a board game similar to bar billiards.

clue.text: Holy one beheaded by mistake

indicators.note: beheaded means the head, or first letter, is removed

parts.note: a holy terror is a badly behaved person, so a holy one is a terror

explanation.surface: A saint was decapitated in error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy one' points to the phrase 'holy terror', a troublesome child.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Note with account of life insurance pay-out

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a version is one person's account of events

explanation.surface: A memo accompanied by a statement about a life policy's payment.
explanation.definitionFit: In insurance a reversion is a sum payable on someone's death, such as a reversionary bonus on a life policy.

clue.text: Elgar's befuddled by drink

indicators.note: befuddled means confused, so the composer's name is jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: The composer Elgar is made tipsy by alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' and gives no letter; 'befuddled' rearranges ELGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, a common alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Widow, about fifty-one, caught here

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals
ct is a cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A widowed woman of about fifty-one is trapped in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' only links the wordplay; CT for caught is a cricket abbreviation alongside the more usual C.
explanation.definitionFit: Relict is an old legal term for a surviving spouse, a woman left behind after her husband died.

clue.text: Girl with a recorder takes the Circle Line

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
a meter is a device that records readings, such as a gas meter

explanation.surface: A girl carrying a tape recorder rides London's Circle Line underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route, but here it is any straight line passing through a circle's centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A diameter is the straight chord running through the centre of a round figure from edge to edge.

clue.text: Girl in car case gets muddled, the hair-brained child

indicators.note: in places the girl's name within the rearranged letters
muddled means mixed up, so the letters of car case are scrambled

parts.note: Peg is a short form of the girl's name Margaret

explanation.surface: A girl inside a mixed-up car case: a scatterbrained youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets muddled' rearranges the letters of car case, and the girl sits inside them. 'Hair-brained' is the printed spelling of hare-brained.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegrace is a reckless rascal, a wild good-for-nothing.

clue.text: It hurts Tom's hands

parts.note: a torture device for the digits, read also as the crew belonging to Tom Thumb, the tiny fairy-tale hero

explanation.surface: Something painful afflicts a man called Tom's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as Tom THUMB'S CREW: the tiny hero's 'hands' are his crew, as in deck hands.
explanation.definitionFit: This medieval instrument of torture crushed the victim's digits, so it certainly hurts the hands.

clue.text: Put emphasis on the Tube?

definitions.meaning: London's Tube is an underground railway

explanation.definitionFit: To underline is to stress; split, it is an under line, a railway route below ground, like London's Tube.

clue.text: Get away from, say, the subject of Mussorgsky's song

indicators.note: say signals that the word for running away is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to flee is to run away from

explanation.surface: Escape from, for instance, what Mussorgsky's song is about.
explanation.walkthrough: Mussorgsky's 'Song of the Flea' sets Mephistopheles' song from Goethe's Faust.
explanation.definitionFit: Mussorgsky wrote a famous comic Song of the Flea about a king's pet insect.

clue.text: Sternly inflict a blow on the City

indicators.note: on means the wind is placed next to the city

parts.note: Auster is the south wind, so a blow
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Harshly delivering a punch to the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the City' suggests London's financial district but is the cathedral city of Ely in eastern England; 'inflict' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerely means in a severe, strict manner.

clue.text: Church put on comic opera, by name The Duenna

indicators.note: comic suggests a farcical treatment, so the letters of opera are scrambled

explanation.surface: A church stages a comic opera named The Duenna.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duenna is indeed a comic opera by Sheridan, which makes the definition look like part of the surface; 'comic' rearranges OPERA into APERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who acts as a chaperon to a young lady in Spain.

clue.text: In this way an American lawer gets a drink

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer (the page misprints lawyer)

explanation.surface: Thus an American attorney buys himself something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'lawer' is a misprint for 'lawyer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water, or in America any fizzy soft beverage, is a common thing to sip.

clue.text: It's dumb having no address

definitions.meaning: unable or too stunned to say anything
read as ..., lacking a formal talk

explanation.definitionFit: Someone struck dumb cannot utter words; split, the word means lacking a speech, an address in the sense of an oration.

clue.text: Row over a royal style of art

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word for row is placed above the rest

parts.note: a row is a line
R stands for royal, as in RN or RAF

explanation.surface: An argument about a regal art style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear art relies on outline and drawing rather than colour and tone.

clue.text: Air transport

definitions.meaning: air in the sense of manner or bearing
conveyance, or a vehicle for passengers

explanation.definitionFit: Carriage means deportment, like an air or bearing, and also the carrying of goods or a horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: Form of elegance

definitions.meaning: a form is a school year group

explanation.definitionFit: A class is a group of pupils, a form, and class also means stylishness.

clue.text: Money for the group cut off

indicators.note: cut off means the word for the group loses its tail letter

parts.note: a species is a group of related organisms

explanation.surface: Funds for the team have been stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is coin as opposed to paper currency.

clue.text: Duct used in Mexican alembic

indicators.note: used in says the letters are found within the two words

explanation.surface: A tube used in a Mexican distilling flask.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal in anatomy is a tube or passage, such as the ear canal.

clue.text: Ivories from the islands

definitions.meaning: low coral islands, as off southern Florida

explanation.definitionFit: Piano notes are struck on keys, and the Florida Keys are a chain of small islands.

clue.text: The players aren't meant to hear this aright, perhaps

definitions.text: The players aren't meant to hear this
definitions.meaning: a theatrical remark addressed to the audience, which by convention the other actors on stage do not hear
read as 'a right', an example of a side, since right is one side

explanation.surface: Actors are not supposed to catch this, if all goes correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's remark to the audience is unheard by the cast; split, the word is a side, as right is one example of one.

clue.text: Straying, a boy's first to go wrong and get the cane perhaps

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word boy's is used

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible variant, so the word cane is jumbled

explanation.surface: A truant boy misbehaves at first and is caned for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CANE into ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrance is a departure from the right path, a wandering from what is usual.

clue.text: Deviate from course and head for port

parts.note: to sheer is to swerve or veer off course, as a ship does
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A ship swerves off course and heads for harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEERNESS is a port town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, at the mouth of the Medway.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheerness in Kent is a commercial harbour town on the Thames estuary.

clue.text: It's not on with this girl of yours, not on any account

definitions.text: It's not on with this girl of yours, not on any account

parts.words: It's not on with this girl of yours, not on any account
parts.note: evokes the British idiom 'not on your ...' followed by a girl's name, meaning certainly not

explanation.surface: A refusal: there is no way this girl is going out with you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on your nelly' is old British slang meaning 'absolutely not', from rhyming slang Nelly Duff for puff, i.e. breath of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl's name completes the idiom of emphatic refusal, never in a million years.
